questions.instructions: Given the alert and its context records, does this describe unauthorized activity, as opposed to authorized activity that a detector flagged?

criteria.true: Someone is doing something they were not authorized to do
criteria.false: The activity was authorized, expected, or did not happen -- administrative work, a sanctioned tool, a test, or a detector firing on nothing

questions.instructions: Do the context records -- tickets, registrations, schedules, authorization excerpts -- account for the flagged activity?

criteria.true: A specific record covers this specific activity: the same actor, asset, or window, authorized in advance
criteria.false: No record covers it, or the records that exist are about something adjacent. Silence is not an explanation

questions.instructions: How strong is the evidence that the activity is unauthorized?
criteria: Speculative: hedged language, or a single weak indicator
Confirmed: direct proof of unauthorized activity

questions.instructions: Have credentials been disclosed to, or captured by, someone unauthorized?

criteria.true: A password, key or token has been submitted to an attacker-controlled destination, or is otherwise in hands it should not be in
criteria.false: No credential has left the control of its owner

questions.instructions: Is a live session or token being used by someone unauthorized right now?

criteria.true: An authenticated session or token is in active use by someone other than the owner
criteria.false: Every active session belongs to the person it was issued to, or none are active

questions.instructions: Is malicious mail sitting in user inboxes at this moment?

criteria.true: A malicious message is still delivered and reachable in one or more mailboxes
criteria.false: Nothing malicious is in any mailbox, or the incident is not about mail

questions.instructions: Is there a mechanism that would survive a reboot and bring the activity back?

criteria.true: A scheduled task, service, startup entry, key or implant placed by the attacker is still in place
criteria.false: Nothing would restart the activity once it stopped

questions.instructions: Is a specific malicious process or task executing right now?

criteria.true: A named process, script or scheduled task is running and doing the harm described
criteria.false: Nothing is executing; the evidence is of something that already ran or never ran

questions.instructions: Is data or command traffic leaving to a destination under attacker control?

criteria.true: An outbound channel to an attacker destination is carrying traffic now
criteria.false: No outbound channel is open, or the destination is legitimate

questions.instructions: Did the attacker create or change a configuration that persists on its own?

criteria.true: Mailbox forwarding rules, delegations, OAuth consents, keys or policy entries were created or altered during the incident
criteria.false: No configuration was changed, or the changes were made by their legitimate owner

questions.instructions: Is the activity live or imminent, rather than finished?

criteria.true: It is happening now, or the evidence points at an imminent next step
criteria.false: It is finished, already remediated, or a historical record of something stopped

questions.instructions: Has this reached beyond the entity that was originally flagged?

criteria.true: A second host, account or mailbox is implicated, or lateral movement is underway
criteria.false: Everything in evidence is confined to the entity that was flagged

criteria.workgroup: A team, a distribution list, or a handful of related assets
criteria.organization_wide: Everyone, or an asset the whole organization depends on

questions.instructions: What kind of attack does the evidence describe?

criteria.host_compromise: Malware, ransomware, or persistence on a host
criteria.account_takeover: Stolen or abused credentials or sessions
criteria.mail_campaign: Phishing or malicious mail sitting in user inboxes
criteria.exfiltration: Data staging or outbound theft in progress
